pillars.kicker: Everything under one key - and one editor on your disk
pillars.notesBlurb: Rich live editor, tags, instant search.
pillars.journalBlurb: Mood, sleep, medication. Research-backed tags, doctor export.
pillars.filesBlurb: Encrypted images, docs, audio, and video.
pillars.bookmarksBlurb: Saved links with website icons. Import your browser bookmarks.
pillars.contactsBlurb: Numbers, emails, addresses. Import your whole address book.
pillars.calendarBlurb: Events and reminders. Day, week, and month views.

mdEditor.title: A free Markdown editor. Your files never leave your disk.
mdEditor.body: Point it at a folder of .md and .txt files - subfolders show up automatically, edits save in place, and nothing is converted. The same rich editor as your notes: live preview, tasks, tags, and tables.
mdEditor.platforms: In the desktop app or any Chromium browser.

meds.tileBlurb: Every dose on a schedule, with a reminder on your phone. Taken, skipped or missed in one tap.
meds.heading: Never miss a dose. Your pills are nobody's business.
meds.intro: Add a medication once, with its dose and its times. Each day asks for one tap: taken, skipped or missed. The reminder rings on your phone. The list, the doses and the skipped days are encrypted on your device, and they stay that way when they sync.
meds.cardScheduleBody: Morning and evening, every other day, once a week, or only when you need it. Each medication keeps its own times.
meds.cardHistoryBody: Raise or lower a dose and the history stays. Your mood before and after the change sits on the same line.
meds.cardRefillBody: Enter the pack size once. The app counts down and names the day to reorder.

ninja.tileBlurb: Press {{key}} and type. A few letters jump anywhere, + makes anything in plain words, > runs a command. Your hands never leave the keyboard.
ninja.placeholder: Type a title, + to add, or > for commands

shots.empty: The empty box lists what you opened last.
shots.find: A few letters find a title, and the line inside a note that holds them.
shots.logins: Logins, cards and bookmarks come up by name, next to your notes.
shots.day: A day in plain words opens the calendar on it, with that day’s journal entry right under it.
shots.folders: / lists your folders with their place in the tree; a new name makes a new folder.
shots.tags: # lists your tags with how many items each holds; / does the same for folders.
shots.settings: Type what you are after, “dark”: the box finds the setting, the command and the line in your notes.
shots.bestmatch: Type a command by its name, “lock app”: it comes first, and Enter runs it.
shots.event: An event typed in plain words: the day, the time and the alert are read out before you press Enter.
shots.repeat: Repeats in plain words: “every friday 4-5pm” becomes a weekly event, read out before you press Enter.
shots.rent: Monthly bills with a reminder the day before, typed the way you would say them.
shots.trip: A trip over several days, filed in your Travel folder in the same line.
shots.exam: A tag and a space in the line file the new item where it belongs.
shots.journal: A type word picks the kind: this line makes a journal entry for tonight.
shots.quotes: Words in quotes stay in the title: “Friday” is not read as a day.
shots.append: Two tasks added to the Packing list from wherever you are.
shots.newlist: A list name that does not exist yet makes the list, with the tasks in it.
shots.link: Paste a link after +: keep it as a bookmark, clip the page as a note, or start a login.
shots.clip: Clip a page: the article and its pictures become a note you keep.
shots.menu: Tab shows the item’s own menu, right in the box.
shots.menufilter: Type in the item’s menu to find the action: pin, archive, move, share.
shots.commands: > lists every command, with its key.
shots.features: > opens with the features: statistics, trackers, medication, a password generator, each with a line on what it does.
shots.theme: Type “theme”: every theme with its colors. Enter wears it, light or dark.

demoShot.caption: The real app with sample notes, right in your browser. Nothing is saved.

downloads.heading: Download PrivacyNotes
downloads.playDesc: Updates through the Play Store. Purchases in the app are billed by Google.
downloads.apkDesc: Every update is a download and an install you do yourself.
downloads.obtainiumDesc: Installs every new release from our repo.
downloads.apkFootnote: Needs Android 7.0 or newer. Zapstore, Obtainium and the APK need no Google account and no Google billing: Pro unlocks via web checkout. The APK alerts you in-app when a new version is ready.
downloads.linuxRequirement: Both formats need webkit2gtk 4.1: Ubuntu 22.04 or newer, Debian 12 or newer, or an equivalent release from 2023 onward. Older distributions only ship webkit2gtk 4.0 and cannot run these builds.
downloads.linuxArchX86Desc: Nearly every desktop and laptop. Pick this if unsure.
downloads.linuxArchArmDesc: Raspberry Pi, ARM laptops, Linux in a VM on an Apple Silicon Mac
downloads.debFootnote: Updating an existing <highlight>.deb install</highlight>? Do not uninstall it first. Double-clicking the file dead-ends in Ubuntu's App Center, which only reports that the app is installed, so install the new one over the old one from a terminal. Use the line that matches your machine; dpkg --print-architecture prints which one you need:
downloads.availability: Available now: macOS 13+, Windows 10+, iOS 17.4+, Linux and Android.
downloads.pkgBrewDesc: brew upgrade skips it: the app updates itself.
downloads.pkgFootnote: Each one installs the same signed build.
downloads.githubNote: Signed · Public · Verifiable · Every single release
downloads.zapstoreDesc: <rec>Recommended.</rec> Verifies our signature before it installs.

mood.heading: Track what you actually feel.
mood.intro: Mood, sleep, medication and more, each a tap a day. Everything is always encrypted, on your device and when it syncs.
mood.cardPatternsBody: Every tracker ranked by what it does to your mood, with the finding written out in plain words.
mood.cardExploreBody: One tracker against your mood, the same day or the next. Sleep tonight, mood tomorrow.
mood.cardMedsBody: Taken or skipped, dose changes on a timeline, and adherence held against your mood.
mood.cardShareBody: A printable report for your doctor, or a structured prompt for an AI. Computed on your device, and nothing leaves it unless you send it.
mood.encryptedBody: Nobody logs their antidepressant dosage in Notion. Nobody tracks hopeless days in a Google Doc. Data this sensitive needs encryption on the device, so that is how PrivacyNotes is built.

whyPrivacy.heading: Write “buy a new TV”. <accent>See TVs for a month.</accent>
whyPrivacy.lead: That is how most free note apps pay their bills: what you write is read, profiled and sold, and the ads come after you.
whyPrivacy.differenceBody: <brand/> encrypts your notes on your device. There are no ads, no pixels, no third-party trackers and no analytics of what you write, and there never will be. The code is open source, so you can check that yourself.
whyPrivacy.keyboardNote: A note on device keyboards. Third-party keyboards (such as Gboard, SwiftKey, or Samsung Keyboard) may send what you type to their own servers. This happens at the operating-system level, outside any app’s control. Consider disabling cloud features in your keyboard settings or using an offline-only keyboard.

readIt.heading: Do not trust us. Read it.
readIt.body: The app you are running is published, along with the encryption inside it. Start with the one-minute check that needs no tools, or go straight to the code.

noRecovery.heading: Your phrase is your key
noRecovery.body: With self-custody, no phrase means no notes: nobody can recover them. That is the trade-off for holding the only key, so writing to our team cannot bring your notes back.
noRecovery.noRecoveryDesc: With self-custody, lose your phrase and you lose your notes
noRecovery.deviceDesc: With self-custody, your phrase never touches our servers
noRecovery.zkDesc: With self-custody, the server holds nothing that opens your notes
noRecovery.printDesc: View and export your phrase any time
noRecovery.googleDesc: We store your key by default, or you back up your own phrase

about.intro: <brand/> keeps your notes, tasks, passwords, journal, files, calendar, contacts and bookmarks in one place, with mood and medication tracking. Everything is encrypted on your device with a key made from your 12 words, and it stays encrypted on our servers in <nowrap>Switzerland</nowrap>. It works offline, and the app is open source.
about.seeWhatsNew: See all changes on PrivacyNotes.app with screenshots
about.tagline: No subscriptions. Just Software. Not a service.
about.singleKeysDesc: Use J, K, Q, / and ?, and T, D, W, M and N in the Calendar, without holding Cmd or Ctrl.

trust.openSourceBody: The app and the encryption inside it are published, so anyone can check how your notes are encrypted.
trust.dataStorageBody: Encrypted blobs stored in Zurich, <flag/> Switzerland.
trust.faviconsBody1: Website icons (favicons) come from DuckDuckGo and Google, fetched by our server on your behalf. Your browser never contacts either one, so they see our server asking for a domain and never see you.
trust.faviconsBody2: Icons are cached on your device for 90 days. No request includes your identity, and you can turn icons off in Settings > Lists.

feedback.title: Send feedback
feedback.intro: Bugs and feature requests go to GitHub, so we can track every one.
feedback.outro: Found a security issue? Use the <contact>private security contact on GitHub</contact>, not a public issue.

rate.title: Give something back
rate.intro: Most people never pay us anything, and that is by design. A rating is a lovely way to say thanks.
rate.outro: We read every review that comes in, and a word from someone who uses this daily is what keeps us going.
